query: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs phase stability and why, with relevance to retaining desirable combinations of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries of the hypothesis, supporting prior evidence, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by the competition between the formation of face-centered cubic (FCC) and body-centered cubic (BCC) phases, which is influenced by the atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration of the constituent elements.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or annealed Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys
generation.intervention: In situ high-pressure synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction to study phase transformations
generation.conditions: High temperatures (up to 1000°C), high pressures (up to 10 GPa), and varying alloy compositions
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration of the constituent elements
generation.mechanism: The atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration of the constituent elements influence the formation of FCC and BCC phases, which in turn affects the phase stability and the resulting properties of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in high-temperature strength and a 30% improvement in environmental resistance compared to the baseline alloy composition, as measured by yield strength and corrosion rate, respectively.
generation.baseline: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy with a composition of Al0.1Co0.1Cr0.2Fe0.3Ni0.3
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is valid for Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys with a composition range of Al0.05-0.2Co0.05-0.2Cr0.1-0.3Fe0.2-0.4Ni0.2-0.4
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the atomic-size difference, valence-electron concentration, and phase stability is not well understood and may be influenced by other factors such as grain size and defects.

falsification_experiment.design: In situ high-pressure synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction experiment to study phase transformations in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys with varying compositions
measurements: Phase fraction, lattice parameter, and yield strength
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the phase stability is not correlated with the atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration, as measured by a correlation coefficient less than 0.5, then the hypothesis is falsified.

frame.limitation: lack of understanding of what governs phase stability in these alloys

precedents.problem: Understanding the properties of high-entropy alloys
precedents.lever: in situ high-pressure synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction
precedents.outcome: Discovery of a polymorphic transition from face-centred-cubic (fcc) structure to hexagonal-close-packing (hcp) structure in the prototype CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy

precedents.problem: Understanding the mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys
precedents.outcome: Demonstration that reducing the Ta level in the refractory TiZrHfTax system destabilizes the body-centered cubic (bcc) phase and leads to the appearance of the hexagonal close-packed (hcp) phase embedded in the bcc matrix

precedents.lever: in situ high-pressure synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction
precedents.outcome: Revelation of a polymorphic transition from face-centred-cubic (fcc) structure to hexagonal-close-packing (hcp) structure in the prototype CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy

precedents.problem: Designing high-entropy alloys with high strength and high ductility
precedents.outcome: Design of an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) with a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure, showing an unprecedented combination of high tensile ductility and high fracture strength at room temperature

precedents.problem: Understanding the damage tolerance of high-entropy alloys
precedents.lever: in situ straining in an aberration-corrected transmission electron microscope
precedents.outcome: Identification of a synergy of multiple deformation mechanisms underlying the origin of the excellent properties of the single-phase CrMnFeCoNi alloy

precedents.problem: Understanding the phase transformation strengthening in high-entropy alloys
precedents.outcome: Connection of the magnetic and mechanical properties of CrCoNi, via a magnetically tunable phase transformation, leading to a fcc-hcp phase transformation that occurs only in this alloy

precedents.problem: Understanding the inverse Hall-Petch behavior in high-entropy alloys
precedents.outcome: Evidence of inverse Hall-Petch behavior for a single-phase high entropy alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) in ultra-high vacuum, associated with low friction coefficients and high wear resistance

precedents.problem: Improving the cryogenic strength of high-entropy alloys
precedents.outcome: Improvement of the cryogenic tensile properties of the CrMnFeCoNi alloy by inducing twinning at room temperature, allowing yield strengths approaching 1 GPa
